Thanks  this is very helpful, Emma. See bullets below and the attached scenario outputs. I ran three scenarios (1M / 3M / 8M tokens) with both on-demand and committed pricing. Highlights: 

- Pricing bands (example): on-demand $18/1M tokens; 3M commit bucket $12/1M; 6M+ commit $10/1M. These are illustrative  final numbers can shift with contract term and throughput.
- Token unit cost calculation: $12/1M -> per-token = $0.000012. Example: conversational summary ~300 tokens/session -> cost per session = $0.0036. For 100k sessions/month thats $360/month of inference cost.
- Per-feature example (Account insights): assume 150 tokens/session avg, 100k sessions/month -> 15M tokens -> (at $10/1M committed) inference cost = $150. Wait check math: 15M tokens at $10 per 1M = $150. (Note: I incorrectly stated  corrected within the model; please see workbook.)

- CAC payback example: if your CA C is $300/customer and ARPU from features is $30/month, with inference contribution-to-cost of $2/customer/month, the payback period is: CAC / (gross margin contribution per month). If we target gross margin contribution of $20/month, CAC payback is 15 months; if we can reduce inference cost or raise ARPU to $40/month, payback drops to ~7.5 months. I'll attach a table that shows payback at different ARPU / CAC combos.

- Margin targets: many of our mid-market customers target gross margins >65	370% after hosting and inference costs. For that, inference should be a relatively small % of ARPU (we show examples at 2	310% of revenue).

Attachments: unit_econ_model.xlsx (model with scenarios) and pricing-sheet.csv (example tier pricing). Also attaching a draft SOW for committed pricing (SOW_draft_v1.pdf) for procurement review if you want to move forward.

Proposed next step: If committed pricing at $10/1M looks viable, we can prepare a 6-month pilot SOW with a 6M token commitment and a step-down schedule. If not, well propose a conservative 3M commit. Happy to review numbers with your finance/procurement team  let me know names and Ill send the SOW + redlines.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
